title: Sherpa UI Figma Composition Spec
description: The FIGMA-IDIOMATIC projection of a composition-map (schema/composition-map.schema.json). This is what the map→figma compiler produces and drives into the Figma bridge (figma_execute), and the low-level target the frame extractor reads. It stays in FIGMA's vocabulary — node kinds, bound variables, mode pins, paint styles, slots — and is deliberately NOT merged with the code view-definition (the 'two schemas + a mapping' decision). It formalises and extends the NODE spec that scripts/figma-component-builder.js already accepts, adding instance-composition (dropping component/pseudo instances into slots and grids). Presentation binds to design-system variables; raw values are a fallback only. See docs/COMPOSITION-MAP.md.

page.description: Target Figma page name the composition frame lives on.

fonts.description: Fonts to loadFontAsync at the top of the build call (they don't persist across figma_execute calls). Each is [family, style].

root.description: The root frame of the composition.

fnode.description: One Figma node in the composition. `kind` selects the node type. Mirrors the builder's NODE shape (frame/text/icon/instance) plus 'slot' and the composition kinds.

kind.description: frame = auto-layout/GRID container. text = text node (via a text style). icon = single-level glyph instance. instance = an instance of a sherpa-* component main (role=component in the map). pseudo = an instance of a reusable non-sherpa Figma component (role=pseudo — arc/bar/gridlines) OR its inline geometry. vector = a raw vector path (role=raw). slot = a SLOT (converted post-hoc via figma_add_slot_property).

componentKey.description: For kind=instance/pseudo: the component main's key to createInstance from (stable across sessions). Preferred over nodeId.

nodeId.description: For kind=instance/pseudo: fallback session-scoped node id of the main, if no key. For any node: the live id for compile-in-place.

instanceProps.description: For kind=instance/pseudo: component property values to set via setProperties — variant axes, boolean props, text props. These are the Figma projection of the map node's `props`, routed per the component's @figma rule. Keys are Figma property names (e.g. 'Variant', 'hasIcon', 'label'); values are strings/booleans.

fill.description: Fill — a bound variable {c,v} or a paint style name {style} or raw {rgba}. null = no fill.

modePins.description: explicitVariableModes to pin on this node (chart series colour, snapping, status). [collection, mode] pairs.

data.description: SVG-ish path data 'M x y L x y …'.

arcData.description: For kind=pseudo arc segments: ellipse arcData {startingAngle, endingAngle, innerRadius} (radians, 0=3 o'clock CW).

slot.description: Mark this frame for conversion to a SLOT (figma_add_slot_property runs post-build).

slotName.description: For kind=slot / slot=true: the slot's name (matches the code component's named slot).

collapseEmpty.description: Empty slots default to 100px and inflate the parent — hug them to ~1px.

visible.description: Node visibility (CSS owns visibility in code; Figma sets it literally).

children.description: Child nodes in normal flow / grid cells. Order preserved. For grid children, position/span come from each child's layout.gridPos.

flayout.description: Figma auto-layout / GRID properties. The Figma projection of the map's neutral `layout`.

gridPos.description: For a child of a GRID: its cell + span. row/col 0-indexed.

padding.description: A single var/px applied to all sides, or per-side {t,b,l,r}.

positioning.description: ABSOLUTE for overlay marks (gridlines/vectors filling a slot).

constraints.description: For ABSOLUTE/overlay nodes: {horizontal, vertical} STRETCH/SCALE so marks scale with the plot.

varRef.description: A bound design-system variable {c: collection, v: prefixed/name} or a raw px number (fallback).

paintRef.description: A fill/stroke source: a bound variable {c,v}, a paint style {style: name}, or raw {rgba:{r,g,b,a}}. null = none.

sides.description: Which side(s) to weight (chart gridlines use one side).
